name.description: Return labels whose name matches this value, compared case-insensitively. Use it to resolve a label name to the id you send in `label_ids`.

parent-id.description: Return only the labels nested under this label. For the opposite view, send `parent_id__isnull=true` to get every top-level label in the project. Use `parent_id__isnull=false` for every label that has a parent.

external-id.description: Return labels whose `external_id` matches. Combine with `external_source` to resolve a record from another system to its Plane label without keeping a local id map.

external-source.description: Return labels that came from this system, for example `github` or `jira`.

search.description: A search term matched against the label `name`. Use it for type-ahead in a picker instead of downloading every page and filtering client-side.

order-by.description: Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. Defaults to `sort_order`. - `sort_order`, `-sort_order`: the project's own label ordering - `created_at`, `-created_at`: oldest or newest first - `id`, `-id` A value outside this list isn't rejected. It falls back to the default `sort_order` without an error, so a typo in `order_by` shows up only as a differently sorted page.

offset.description: Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read the `next` value from the response and send it back as `offset` to walk forward.

paginate.description: Set to `cursor` to switch from the default offset envelope to the keyset cursor envelope, which skips the `COUNT(*)` and returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Send the returned `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the following page. Only `created_at` and `id` are cursor-eligible, because a keyset needs a strictly ordered column and `sort_order` is neither unique nor monotonic. Pair `paginate=cursor` with `order_by=created_at` or `order_by=id`. With the default `sort_order` ordering, the request returns `400 ordering_not_cursor_eligible`. Most projects have few enough labels that the default offset envelope is all you need.

count.description: Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to omit `total_count` and skip the count query.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Fields you don't request are left out of the response instead of coming back as `null`, so a missing key means you didn't ask for it and `null` means the value is null. `id` is always included, whether or not you name it. Pass `all` to get every requestable field. An unknown field name returns `400` with the list of valid names and the closest match, so a typo is caught instead of being silently ignored. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `sort_order`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`. See [Sparse fields](/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields).
